rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One definition makes a blessing a benefit bestowed as kindness upon another.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن المنفعة المفعولة على جهة الإحسان إلى الغير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another definition adds that the benefit must be good, since only a good act merits gratitude.
rows.anchor: المنفعة الحسنة المفعولة على جهة الإحسان إلى الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects requiring the benefit to be good: gratitude for kindness and blame for sin concern different aspects and can coexist.
rows.anchor: هذا القيد غير معتبر لأنه يجوز أن يستحق الشكر بالإحسان وإن كان فعله محظورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pure harm is not a blessing, because the definition requires a benefit.
rows.anchor: أما قولنا المنفعة فلأن المضرة المحضة لا تكون نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver must intend kindness to the recipient; an apparent benefit pursued for the giver's own profit is not a blessing.
rows.anchor: لو كان نفعا حقا وقصد الفاعل به نفع نفسه لا نفع المفعول به لا يكون نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every benefit or removal of harm reaching creatures is ultimately from God, and blessings fall into three categories.
rows.anchor: أن كل ما يصل إلى الخلق من النفع ودفع الضرر فهو من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some blessings appear to come through another person, but God creates the gift, recipient, and benefactor's impulse; the human instrument is thanked while God is the true benefactor.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه تعالى لما أجرى تلك النعمة على يد ذلك العبد كان ذلك العبد مشكورا ولكن المشكور في الحقيقة هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benefits received through obedience also come from God, who enables, assists, guides, and removes obstacles; therefore all blessings are truly from Him.
rows.anchor: لولا أن الله سبحانه وتعالى وفقنا للطاعات وأعاننا عليها وهدانا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is God's first blessing: nothing can be enjoyed without life, and the Qur'an mentions bringing people to life before worldly provisions.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن أصل جميع النعم هو الحياة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of Razi's Ash'arite colleagues deny that God bestows any blessing on unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض أصحابنا ليس لله تعالى على الكافر نعمة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites affirm that God gives unbelievers both religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : لله على الكافر نعمة دينية ونعمة دنيويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supports his colleagues: if unbelievers were among those favored, asking for the favored path would ask for their path; calling the phrase appositional to the straight path does not remove that consequence.
rows.anchor: فكان التقدير اهدنا صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم وحينئذ يعود المحذور المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi also cites the verse saying unbelievers' respite increases their sin as evidence against calling their worldly lot a blessing.
rows.anchor: إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly benefits are negligible beside everlasting afterlife punishment, as a small sweetness is not counted a benefit when mixed with much poison.
rows.anchor: نعم الدنيا في مقابلة عذاب الآخرة على الدوام قليلة كالقطرة في البحر

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The opposing evidence includes the command that all people worship their creator, who prepared the earth and sky for them, presenting these as universal blessings.
rows.anchor: فنبه على أنه يجب على الكل طاعة الله لمكان هذه النعم العظيمة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They also cite God's bringing people to life as an act of grace, His reminder to Israel of His favor, and statements that few give thanks as evidence that blessings reach unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وشرح النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means asking for the path of those favored; 4:69 identifies them as prophets and the truthful, whose chief is Abu Bakr, so it supports his imamate and the propriety of following him.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن رأس الصديقين ورئيسهم أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor cannot mean worldly benefits; it means religious favor, and among these faith alone can exist without the other religious gifts.
rows.anchor: ولما بطل الأول ثبت أن المراد منه نعمة الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi therefore identifies the favor in the verse specifically as faith.
rows.anchor: فرجع حاصل القول في قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم أنه طلب لنعمة الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is explicitly the giver of faith, He creates and grants it; otherwise the servant would bestow the greatest blessing and God's praise of His own favor would be misplaced, against the Mu'tazilites.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن خالق الإيمان والمعطي للإيمان هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer cannot remain eternally in Hell, since the verse praises this gift as a great favor; a favor with no effect on endless punishment would be insignificant.
rows.anchor: يجب أن لا يبقى المؤمن مخلدا في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not obligated to provide the best religious guidance: a required act would not count as a favor, whereas the verse calls it one.
rows.anchor: لا يجب على الله رعاية الصلاح والأصلح في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor cannot merely mean giving capacity, guidance, or removing excuses, since these are also given to unbelievers while the verse singles out some people.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك حاصل في حق الكفار

rows.speaker: المشهور
rows.claim: The commonly reported identification makes those under wrath the Jews and those astray the Christians, citing the Qur'an's descriptions of each.
rows.anchor: المشهور أن المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls this restricted identification weak, since deniers of the Creator and polytheists have worse creeds and should more obviously be disavowed.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف ؛ لأن منكري الصانع والمشركين أخبث دينا من اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader reading takes those under wrath as people who err in outward deeds, including sinners, and those astray as people who err in belief; the wording is general and should not be restricted without cause.
rows.anchor: المغضوب عليهم على كل من أخطأ في الأعمال الظاهرة وهم الفساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi also offers a possible reading in which those under wrath are unbelievers and those astray are hypocrites, following the order of groups in the opening of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال : المغضوب عليهم هم الكفار والضالون هم المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God has judged a group astray, they cannot also be believers, since that would turn God's truthful report into a lie.
rows.anchor: امتنع كونهم مؤمنين وإلا لزم انقلاب خبر الله الصدق كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the immunity of prophets and angels from actions or beliefs contrary to the favored path: otherwise they would stray and could not be models or belong among those favored.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذلك باطلا علمنا بهذه الآية عصمة الأنبياء والملائكة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human anger is a bodily change, impossible for God; psychological terms applied to God signify their final effect, so divine anger means willing harm, while divine modesty means leaving an act.
rows.anchor: لفظ الغضب في حق الله تعالى لا يحمل على أوله الذي هو غليان دم القلب بل على غايته الذي هو إرادة الإضرار

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that divine anger proves people freely chose their sins, or God's anger would be unjust.
rows.anchor: غضب الله عليهم يدل على كونهم فاعلين للقبائح باختيارهم

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's Ash'arite school reads the sequence as God's anger causing their misguidance; the reverse would make a human attribute affect God, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: دل ذلك على أن غضب الله عليهم علة لكونهم ضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah begins by praising God and ends by censuring those who reject faith and obedience, showing that turning to God brings good while turning away brings affliction.
rows.anchor: مطلع الخيرات وعنوان السعادات هو الإقبال على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse divides people into the obedient who are favored, sinners under wrath, and those ignorant of religion or unbelievers who are astray.
rows.anchor: أن المكلفين ثلاث فرق : أهل الطاعة وإليهم الإشارة بقوله : أنعمت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinners are mentioned before unbelievers because everyone avoids unbelief, while people may fail to guard against sin, making the warning about sin more pressing.
rows.anchor: لأن كل واحد يحترز عن الكفر أما قد لا يحترز عن الفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi poses the problem that divine anger follows knowledge of human sin: if God's knowledge is eternal, why create people destined for endless punishment and why create what He is angry with?
rows.anchor: فهذا العلم إما أن يقال إنه قديم أو محدث فإن كان هذا العلم قديما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If that knowledge is new, God would be subject to temporal events and its creation would require a prior knowledge indefinitely; Razi answers that God does what He wills.
rows.anchor: وجوابه يفعل الله ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the favored cannot also be under wrath or astray, naming the rejected groups adds hope and fear: the first phrase gives complete hope, the latter phrases complete fear, completing faith.
rows.anchor: فقوله صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم يوجب الرجاء الكامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with complete favor unite knowledge of truth for its own sake with doing good for its own sake; lacking practice makes sinners under wrath, while lacking knowledge makes people astray.
rows.anchor: فإن اختل قيد العمل فهم الفسقة وهم المغضوب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This world is obscure and the afterlife pure: worldly realities need an afterlife original, while afterlife realities need a worldly example, or they would be empty illusion or unsupported claim.
rows.anchor: عالم الدنيا عالم الكدورة وعالم الآخرة عالم الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual realm has ranks and one supreme being obeyed by the others; correspondingly, the human realm has one supreme person, with the former as source and the latter as manifestation.
rows.anchor: فالمطاع في عالم الأرواح هو المصدر والمطاع في عالم الأجسام هو المظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual messenger and human messenger meet and correspond, and together complete happiness in the afterlife and this world.
rows.anchor: والمظهر هو الرسول البشري وبهما يتم أمر السعادات في الآخرة وفي الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human messenger's call to God requires seven matters in 2:285–286: four concern knowledge of the origin, two concern servitude, and one concerns return to God.
rows.anchor: فابتداء الأمر أربعة وفي الوسط صار اثنين وفي النهاية صار واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four matters of origin are knowledge of God, angels, books, and messengers, including not distinguishing among God's messengers.
rows.anchor: وهي معرفة الله والملائكة والكتب والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two aspects of servitude are hearing and obeying as the starting point, then seeking forgiveness through trust and complete reliance on God rather than one's own works.
rows.anchor: وأما الكمال فهو التوكل على الله والالتجاء بالكلية إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven petitions of 2:286 map onto the seven Fatiha phrases: protection from forgetfulness to the opening remembrance, burden to praise, and inability to mercy, through forgiveness, worship and aid, guidance, and refuge from the rejected paths.
rows.anchor: وهو المراد من قوله غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven ranks at the end of al-Baqara were revealed to Muhammad in the spiritual realm during the ascent and expressed as al-Fatiha when he descended.
rows.anchor: ذكرها محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام في عالم الروحانيات عند صعوده إلى المعراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting al-Fatiha in prayer sends the lights from manifestation back to their source, mirroring their descent to Muhammad; hence prayer is the believer's ascent.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأها في صلاته صعدت هذه الأنوار من المظهر إلى المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three original satanic entrances are desire, anger, and caprice: animalistic, predatory, and satanic respectively; anger is worse than desire, and caprice worse than anger.
rows.anchor: الشهوة بهيمية والغضب سبعية والهوى شيطانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer's prohibition of indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression addresses the effects of desire, anger, and caprice respectively.
rows.anchor: المراد منه آثار الغضب وقوله : ﴿ والبغي ﴾

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report distinguishes three kinds of wrongdoing: shirk that is never forgiven, harm between people that is not left unaddressed, and self-wrong that God may forgive; Razi associates them with caprice, anger, and desire.
rows.anchor: الظلم ثلاثة : فظلم لا يغفر وظلم لا يترك وظلم عسى الله أن يتركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire produces greed and stinginess, anger produces vanity and pride, and caprice produces unbelief and innovation; their combination produces envy, the worst human trait.
rows.anchor: فالحرص والبخل نتيجة الشهوة والعجب والكبر نتيجة الغضب والكفر والبدعة نتيجة الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy closes the catalogue of human evils as satanic whispering closes satanic evils; Razi repeats a story in which Iblis tells Pharaoh that the envious are worse than either of them.
rows.anchor: ولهذا السبب ختم الله مجامع الشرور الإنسانية بالحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha has seven verses to counter these seven vices; its opening three names answer the three basic vices, and the Qur'an and moral traits branch from these foundations.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى سورة الفاتحة وهي سبع آيات لحسم هذه الآفات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God turns one away from caprice, treated as a rival deity; a saying to Moses urges resisting desire because it contests God's sovereignty.
rows.anchor: يا موسى خالف هواك فإني ما خلقت خلقا نازعني في ملكي إلا الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God as the Merciful removes anger, which arises from seeking rule; sovereignty belongs to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: ومن عرف أنه رحمن لا يغضب لأن منشأ الغضب طلب الولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God as Merciful calls a person to imitate mercy and so avoid self-wrong and animalistic behavior.
rows.anchor: ومن عرف أنه رحيم وجب أن يتشبه به في كونه رحيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names Lord and King are close to Merciful and All-Merciful; the three names in the closing surah answer desire, anger, and caprice in that order.
rows.anchor: التقدير كأنه قيل : إن أتاك الشيطان من قبل الشهوة فقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآيات السبع دافعة لتلك الأخلاق القبيحة السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha gathers what people need to know about the origin, the middle of servitude, and the return; Razi begins its proof of the Creator from human creation, citing Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: في تقرير أن سورة الفاتحة جامعة لكل ما يحتاج الإنسان إليه في معرفة المبدأ والوسط والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly establishes the Creator by reflecting on human creation: Abraham says his Lord gives life and death and created him, and Moses says his Lord gave each thing its form and guided it.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses human creation to prove the Creator, as in the command to worship the Lord who created people and the first revelation about creating humanity from a clot.
rows.anchor: استدل بخلق الإنسان على وجود الصانع تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof from creation is also a blessing: it teaches the servant that God exists and gives a great benefit, so it is both evidence and grace.
rows.anchor: فهذه الحالة من حيث أنها تعرف العبد وجود الإله دليل ومن حيث أنها نفع عظيم وصل من الله إلى العبد إنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied organs formed from similar semen show that a knowing, powerful Creator deliberately shapes them for human interests through mercy, making Him worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: تولد الأعضاء المختلفة الطبائع والصور والأشكال من النطفة المتشابهة الأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Praise belongs to God” indicates the Creator's existence, knowledge, power, mercy, perfect wisdom, and entitlement to praise and glorification.
rows.anchor: يدل على وجود الصانع وعلى علمه وقدرته ورحمته وكمال حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord of the worlds” signifies that God is one, owns all worlds, and is the only deity and object of worship.
rows.anchor: ليس في العالم إله سواه ولا معبود غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The All-Merciful, the Merciful” describes the one God as completely merciful and generous before, during, and after death.
rows.anchor: موصوف بكمال الرحمة والكرم والفضل والإحسان قبل الموت وعند الموت وبعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Master of the Day of Judgment” implies resurrection, which wisdom and mercy require to distinguish good from evil and vindicate the wronged.
rows.anchor: أن يحصل بعد هذا اليوم يوم آخر يظهر فيه تمييز المحسن عن المسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant's obligations comprise the act of worship and recognition that worship is only possible with God's aid; the latter opens the question of determinism and free will.
rows.anchor: الأعمال التي يأتي بها العبد والآثار المتفرعة على تلك الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The effects of worship are guidance, unveiling, and disclosure, expressed in the request to be guided to the straight path.
rows.anchor: فهي حصول الهداية والانكشاف والتجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored are complete in knowledge and practice, the condemned neglect righteous deeds, and the astray lack sound belief; asking for the favored path seeks the example of the sound group.
rows.anchor: ثم إن أهل العالم ثلاث طوائف : الطائفة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge grows through one's own reasoning or through receiving predecessors' discoveries: “guide us” asks for the first, and the path of the favored for the second.
rows.anchor: وقوله : ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ إشارة إلى القسم الأول

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a divine report transmitted by the Prophet, God responds to each Fatiha phrase: the opening remembers Him, praise praises Him, the mercy names magnify Him, Judgment Day glorifies Him or is entrusted to Him, worship belongs to Him, aid relies on Him, and guidance is the servant's request.
rows.anchor: فإذا قال العبد : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يقول الله تعالى ذكرني عبدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Fatiha “prayer” shows that religious law serves human interests: people most need knowledge of God's lordship and servitude, which the surah's two halves provide to fulfill the covenant.
rows.anchor: مدار الشرائع على رعاية مصالح الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God names the Fatiha “prayer,” prayer without its recitation does not occur; Razi takes this to establish that reciting it is a pillar, as his school holds.
rows.anchor: أن عند عدم قراءة الفاتحة وجب أن لا تحصل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supports obligatory Fatiha recitation because the Prophet consistently recited it and commands require following him.
rows.anchor: صلوا كما رأتيموني أصلي . وثانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rightly guided caliphs also consistently recited it, and the Prophet commanded Muslims to follow their sunna.
rows.anchor: أن الخلفاء الراشدين واظبوا على قراءتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims everywhere recite it in prayer, and the Qur'an commands following the path of believers.
rows.anchor: أن جميع المسلمين شرقا وغربا لا يصلون إلا بقراءة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophetic statement “no prayer without the Opening of the Book” directly supports the requirement.
rows.anchor: لا صلاة إلا بفاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite what is easy from the Qur'an is obligatory; because reciting other passages is not, the obligatory recitation must be the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وظاهره الوجوب فكانت قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن واجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Fatiha is the safer course, following the prophetic instruction to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
rows.anchor: أن قراءة الفاتحة أحوط فوجب المصير إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's constant practice makes abandoning his command forbidden, and Muslims agree that the Fatiha is better and more complete than another recitation.
rows.anchor: وسابعها : أن الرسول عليه السلام واظب على قراءتها فوجب أن يكون العدول عنه محرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the superior prayer with the Fatiha discharges the obligation, it does not follow that the inferior prayer with another passage does; the obligation remains due.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم من الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الكامل الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الناقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer seeks remembrance of the heart, and this concise surah gathers lordship and servitude and is equated with the mighty Qur'an; nothing else can replace it.
rows.anchor: المقصود من الصلاة حصول ذكر القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted report itself says that prayer is not established without the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الخبر الذي رويناه يدل على أن عند فقدان الفاتحة لا تحصل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the servant remembers God through the opening, God remembers him in turn, as promised in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: لما أقدم العبد على ذكر الله لا جرم ذكره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance is a high and honored form of worship: God repeatedly commands abundant remembrance and praises those who remember in every posture and when resisting Satan.
rows.anchor: أن مقام الذكر مقام عال شريف في العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report supports taking “Allah” as a proper name for God's unique essence, since a derived general noun could not identify that individual essence; “All-Merciful” and “Merciful” are universal terms.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن قولنا الله اسم علم لذاته المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that God says “my servant praised Me” shows that praise is higher than remembrance.
rows.anchor: هذا يدل على أن مقام الحمد أعلى من مقام الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise frames creation: the angels speak of it before Adam is created, and the inhabitants of Paradise end their invocation with it.
rows.anchor: وآخر كلام يذكر بعد فناء العالم هو الحمد أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mind cannot contemplate God's essence: one cannot conceive His true nature, and the Prophet instead directs people to contemplate creation.
rows.anchor: تفكروا في الخلق ولا تفكروا في الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemplating creatures reveals more mercy, favor, and beneficence than evil, because good is essential and evil incidental; therefore praise and thanks predominate.
rows.anchor: أن الخير مطلوب بالذات والشر بالعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that “the All-Merciful, the Merciful” magnifies God differs from the opening formula because praise and Lord of the worlds first establish God's perfection, uniqueness, and beneficence; the mercy names then describe the highest conceivable perfection.
rows.anchor: فلما قال بعده الرحمن الرحيم دل ذلك على أن الإله الكامل في ذاته المكمل لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Master of Judgment glorifies and purifies Him from injustice: the worldly dominance of oppressors and comfort of wrongdoers would contradict mercy without resurrection, vindication, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: أما لما حصل يوم الجزاء ويوم الدين اندفع وهم الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that worship and aid belong between God and servant expresses determinism: a balanced capacity acts only when a decisive motive tips it, and that motive must be created by God.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه غير مستقل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating a decisive motive without an opposing one is God's aid; the request not to let hearts swerve means not creating motives toward false belief and corrupt action, while mercy creates motives to good.
rows.anchor: فخلق تلك الداعية الخالصة عن المعارض هو الإعانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's share is creating the decisive motive; the servant's share is that the action issues from him when capacity and motive coincide, a subtle account of agency.
rows.anchor: أما الذي منه فهو خلق الداعية الجازمة وأما الذي من العبد فهو أن عند حصول مجموع القدرة والداعية يصدر الأثر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree about theology, prophecy, and resurrection despite comparable intellect and sustained inquiry; few reach the truth, so divine guidance must make truth attractive and falsehood repellent.
rows.anchor: الشبهات غالبة والظلمات مستولية ولم يصل إلى كنه الحق إلا القليل القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not intend to believe falsehood; if choice alone controlled belief, no one would err, yet most go astray, showing that reaching truth depends on God's guidance.
rows.anchor: ولما رأينا الأكثرين غرقوا في بحر الضلالات علمنا أن الوصول إلى الحق ليس إلا بهداية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels and prophets likewise attribute knowledge and guidance to God: Razi cites the angels, Adam, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, and Muhammad as examples.
rows.anchor: أما الملائكة فقالوا : ﴿ سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven Fatiha verses correspond to the seven bodily prayer acts—standing, bowing, rising, first prostration, rising between prostrations, second prostration, and sitting—as soul to body.
rows.anchor: أن آيات الفاتحة سبع والأعمال المحسوسة أيضا في الصلاة سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening formula corresponds to standing: the connected letter bāʾ remains upright, and both the formula and standing begin the acts of prayer and other important matters.
rows.anchor: حصلت المناسبة بين التسمية وبين القيام من هذه الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise corresponds to bowing: gratitude looks both to God and His gift, a middle state between turning away and absorption, as bowing lies between standing and prostration; abundant gifts also weigh the back down.
rows.anchor: والركوع حالة متوسطة بين القيام وبين السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy names correspond to rising from bowing, as God's mercy raises the servant after humility; the Prophet says God looks mercifully when the servant praises Him while rising.
rows.anchor: العبد لما تضرع إلى الله في الركوع فيليق برحمته أن يرده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Master of Judgment corresponds to the first prostration: awareness of God's might and majesty produces fear and the deepest humility.
rows.anchor: وذلك يوجب الخوف الشديد فيليق به الإتيان بغاية الخضوع والخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship recalls the preceding prostration while seeking aid asks God to grant success in reaching the second; both match the sitting between prostrations.
rows.anchor: إياك نعبد إخبار عن السجدة التي تقدمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for guidance to the straight path corresponds to the second prostration, because the greatest request fits the greatest humility.
rows.anchor: فهو سؤال لأهم الأشياء فيليق به السجدة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored path corresponds to sitting: after utmost humility God honors the servant by seating him before Him, a great favor; the Prophet's ascension and words of greeting model this believer's ascent.
rows.anchor: وهو أن أمره بالقعود بين يديه وذلك إنعام عظيم من الله على العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven Fatiha verses are the soul of the seven prayer acts, themselves the soul of seven stages of human formation; God is the soul of souls and light of lights.
rows.anchor: روح الأرواح ونور الأنوار هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's ascent has a bodily journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and then the high kingdom, and a spiritual journey from the visible to the unseen and from the unseen to the unseen of the unseen.
rows.anchor: أما ما يتعلق بعالم الأرواح فله معراجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual ascent rises through human spirits, the spirits of the heavens, angels, throne-bearers, and pure spirits detached from bodies, whose worship and love of God exceed human comprehension.
rows.anchor: ثم تترقى فتنتهي إلى الأرواح المقدسة عن التعلقات بالأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent continues through ever-higher spiritual ranks until God, the source of all good and mercy; thus the spirit-world is the unseen and God's presence the unseen of the unseen.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن عالم الأرواح هو عالم الغيب وحضرة جلال الربوبية هي غيب الغيب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God has seventy veils of light; if unveiled, the splendor of His face would burn everything perceived by sight, and only prophetic light reveals the number.
rows.anchor: إن لله سبعين حجابا من النور لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه كل ما أدرك البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer was given to Muhammad as a gift for his community because it joins bodily ascent through actions with spiritual ascent through remembrances.
rows.anchor: إن تحفة أمتك الصلاة وذلك لأنها جامعة بين المعراج الجسماني وبين المعراج الروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break.
rows.anchor: فإنه إذا استحكمت المرافقة تعذرت المفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the hands signals leaving both worlds and directing all inner faculties toward God; “God is greatest” means He exceeds all beings, knowledge, comparison, and even the claim that He is simply greater.
rows.anchor: فاقطع نظرك عنهما بالكلية ووجه قلبك وروحك وسرك وعقلك وفهمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening glorification reveals the lights of divine majesty and moves from declaring God's transcendence to praising Him.
rows.anchor: ثم قل : سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وفي هذا المقام تجلى لك نور سبحات الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Blessed is Your name” unveils pre-eternity and eternity, since blessing here indicates abiding beyond extinction and nonexistence.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله تبارك إشارة إلى الدوام المنزه عن الإفناء والإعدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Exalted is Your majesty” signifies that God's knowledge and greatness exceed every stated measure.
rows.anchor: أعلم وأعظم من أن تكون صفات جلاله ونعوت كماله محصورة في القدر المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no god but You” means every attribute of majesty and perfection belongs only to God; ultimately reason, speech, understanding, and imagination fail before Him.
rows.anchor: كل صفات الجلال وسمات الكمال له لا لغيره
